fixes.explanation: No wall shows up anywhere in this passage, friend. The Jordan River is described as bordering that land (Deuteronomy 3:17), and Moses says, "All your men of valor are to cross over, armed for battle, ahead of your brothers, the Israelites." His order is about crossing the river, not building along it. Nobody gets handed a trowel in this passage.

That's not what Moses says. He commands the men of valor to cross over, armed for battle. About the wives, children and livestock, he says they "…may remain in the cities I have given you…" So staying is allowed for them, not crossing required.

That's right. Moses commands the men of valor to cross over, armed for battle. But he says the wives, children and livestock "…may remain in the cities I have given you…" He even adds, "I know that you have much livestock." The families and herds are allowed to stay put.

Yes. Moses says the families and herds may remain "…until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as He has to you, and they too have taken possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan." These tribes already have rest, and their brothers are still waiting for theirs. Moses ties it to two things, the rest and the brothers taking possession, and he doesn't name a day.

Wisdom is a good thing to want, but it isn't the word in this verse. Moses says the LORD gives "…rest to your brothers as He has to you…" The brothers are waiting on rest and on land. A smarter brain isn't on the list.

Joshua does show up in this passage, but not for this. Moses tells these men that after their brothers have taken possession of their land, "…each of you may return to the possession I have given you." Nothing in that verse says these men stay on under anyone. Joshua gets his own word from Moses a verse later.

Moses tells Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God Himself will fight for you." Joshua is the one Moses is speaking to, and the kingdoms are ones he's "…about to enter." Moses also reminds him, "Your own eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings." So the reason isn't how strong Joshua is. It's who is fighting.

Moses never compares the armies, friend. The reason he gives is that "…the LORD your God Himself will fight for you." He points Joshua to what the LORD has already done to the two kings, not to how many soldiers Israel has.

Nothing here says they've surrendered. Moses calls them kingdoms Joshua is "…about to enter." and tells him not to be afraid of them. The reason he gives is that "…the LORD your God Himself will fight for you." That's the whole reason on the table.

Moses asks, "Please let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan…" He also names the pleasant hill country and Lebanon. Right before that, he calls the LORD's works great and mighty. I think wanting to see the land after all of that is a very human thing.
Moses doesn't ask for another battle. He has already mentioned what the LORD did to "these two kings" (Deuteronomy 3:21). What he asks for is to cross over and see the good land.

The LORD tells Moses, "Go to the top of Pisgah and look to the west and north and south and east. See the land with your own eyes…" That's four directions to look. Moses can't walk in, but he does get to see the land with his own eyes.

The LORD says, "But commission Joshua, encourage him, and strengthen him…" Moses won't be crossing, but he still has a job to do for the man who will. I think that's a kind way to hand things off. He gets to cheer on the guy who will cross ahead of the people.

Writing things down is a fine job, but it isn't the order here. The LORD tells Moses to "…commission Joshua, encourage him, and strengthen him…" The order in this passage is about a person, not a notebook.

No tribe blessings in this passage, friend. Moses does give land to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh earlier in it. But the LORD's order about Joshua is to "…commission Joshua, encourage him, and strengthen him…"

Rebuilding is a fair guess for a leader, but it isn't the word in this verse. The LORD says Joshua will "…enable them to inherit the land that you will see." The word is inherit. It's something the people receive.
